style.visual_cues: Build a continuous visual system from a few shapes and limited colors with deliberate proportions and centers of gravity. Use repetition, division, merging, rotation, and varied timing; let each state lead into the next. Avoid unrelated particles or light effects that weaken the structural motif.
style.note: The source directly names or describes this visual direction.

recommended_stack.purpose: Primary pipeline for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. Visual construction and motion design remain owned by the selected style renderer and motion engine.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP

recommended_stack.style_application: Compose the output of the selected visual and motion layers. Supply seekable time or integrate baked assets; do not replace the style-specific rendering or motion method with framework defaults.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: Use HyperFrames by default. Fall back to Remotion only when the documented fallback condition is met, and record the reason. Do not mix framework APIs.

recommended_stack.name: SVG

recommended_stack.style_application: Apply this tool to Abstract Motion Graphics according to visual_cues and tech.implementation.

recommended_stack.style_application: Apply this tool to Abstract Motion Graphics according to visual_cues and tech.implementation.

recommended_stack.name: @remotion/shapes

recommended_stack.name: Remotion
recommended_stack.runtime: React in browser; rendering orchestrated by Node.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Conditional fallback pipeline for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. Visual construction and motion design remain owned by the selected style renderer and motion engine.
recommended_stack.style_application: Compose the output of the selected visual and motion layers. Supply seekable time or integrate baked assets; do not replace the style-specific rendering or motion method with framework defaults.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.

recommended_stack.name: Motion
recommended_stack.runtime: browser; motion/react for mounted React components
recommended_stack.purpose: Optional animation of DOM or SVG layers for Abstract Motion Graphics. Preserve the style-specific timing and visual cues; verify deterministic video seeking before use.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. Motion is an optional layer, not a drop-in replacement for the HyperFrames GSAP timeline contract. Explicitly synchronize and verify seeking; use GSAP when that integration is not established. Use motion/react only within a React component runtime.

recommended_stack.name: chroma.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally validate colors, derive controlled palette variants, interpolate colors, and check foreground/background contrast.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Start with task-provided colors and the style visual_cues. Keep a shared, deterministic palette and named color tokens. Generate gradients or interpolate colors only when the style permits them; keep limited-palette, monochrome, pixel, and print treatments discrete where required. Evaluate animated color from shared composition time. Check contrast against the actual composited background; a two-color ratio alone does not verify text over transparency, gradients, textures, or video. Pass output through the selected renderer's color API and preserve its color-space handling. Native CSS/SVG colors remain sufficient when no color processing is needed.
recommended_stack.style_application: Read palette.tokens, palette.constraints and palette.agent_instruction for Abstract Motion Graphics. Validate approved colors and assess readable existing token pairs with chroma-js. Use palette.gradient only when enabled and appropriate. Preserve task/reference colors exactly; optional suggested tokens are fallback inputs, not permission to recolor assets.

recommended_stack.name: mo.js
recommended_stack.runtime: browser DOM and SVG; initialize after target elements are mounted
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally generate and animate geometric shapes, radial bursts, swirl accents and existing HTML elements for expressive 2D motion graphics.
recommended_stack.import_guidance: Import mojs from '@mojs/core' using a compatible bundler or the documented browser build. Verify exports and signatures against the installed version. Keep DOM-dependent construction out of server-side rendering.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Use mo.js as an optional effects layer, not a video renderer or replacement for the HyperFrames timeline registration contract. Build effects once, pause independent playback, and evaluate normalized setProgress values from shared seekable composition time. Account explicitly for local start, delay, duration, repeats, yoyo and end visibility using the installed API. Preserve the registered GSAP timeline as the HyperFrames clock and synchronize mo.js through the selected framework update mechanism; verify updates on direct seeks rather than relying only on playback callbacks. For Remotion, use its mounted browser lifecycle and frame-derived time. Assign each animated property one owner; use nested wrappers if GSAP controls scene placement while mo.js controls an inner effect.
recommended_stack.determinism_guidance: Resolve random particle properties into explicit reproducible values before building the effect. Do not regenerate random values with generate() during export or depend on live click triggers. Keep effect state derivable from requested time. Verify initial visibility, direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks against sequential playback, including delays and end holds. If the chosen mo.js effect cannot be reliably evaluated this way, recreate it with the existing GSAP/SVG route rather than introducing a separate playback clock.
recommended_stack.color_guidance: Use the resolved palette tokens directly for stroke and fill. Keep limited and monochrome palettes discrete. Animate color interpolation only when the style and palette permit it; do not adopt example-code colors or add arbitrary particle hues. Preserve typography, approved assets and material treatment.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: Choose mo.js when its shape, burst or swirl modules simplify a meaningful effect. Existing GSAP or native SVG can remain sufficient. Supported shape-property animation does not establish arbitrary path morphing, fluid physics, handwriting, character rigging, frame-by-frame drawing or automatic music analysis.
recommended_stack.style_application: Optional coordinated Shape, ShapeSwirl and Burst sequences within the limited geometric system. Let effects develop the central motif rather than adding unrelated visual noise.

recommended_stack.name: Delaunator
recommended_stack.runtime: JavaScript in browser or Node.js; DOM-independent geometry computation
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally compute Delaunay triangle connectivity, neighboring half-edges and the convex hull of 2D points for mesh-based artwork or spatial visualization. Rendering and motion are supplied separately.
recommended_stack.import_guidance: Import Delaunator from 'delaunator' as an ES module. Supply flat coordinates [x0, y0, x1, y1, ...] to the constructor, preferably a suitable typed array, or point pairs to Delaunator.from(). Verify the installed version and data structures before implementation.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Read triangle vertex indices in groups of three and use the original point coordinates to build SVG polygons, Canvas paths, PixiJS geometry or an appropriate Three.js BufferGeometry. Keep DOM and renderer operations in the browser; Node.js can prepare or cache geometry. Assign palette colors through stable point or face identities, not transient triangle-array positions when retriangulating. Preserve the selected renderer coordinate system, winding, normals and material handling.
recommended_stack.animation_guidance: Derive point positions from shared seekable composition time, with deterministic initial coordinates and no unseeded randomness. For stable deformation, triangulate once and keep indices fixed, while checking for inverted or degenerate faces. For deliberate dynamic triangulation, update coordinates and recompute at the evaluated time, accepting that edges and face identities may switch. Design or cache those changes; do not assume update() preserves connectivity. Verify repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks, boundaries, color continuity and triangle quality. Keep HyperFrames primary and Remotion under its existing fallback condition.
recommended_stack.input_guidance: Use finite 2D coordinates and inspect duplicate, collinear or nearly coincident inputs. Delaunator.from() skips duplicate points; retain an explicit mapping when input identity matters. Do not assume every input creates a useful triangle. Geographic inputs need a suitable projection or a spherical triangulation tool rather than treating longitude and latitude as a universally valid planar distance system.
recommended_stack.limitations: This is unconstrained 2D point triangulation, not arbitrary 3D surface meshing, polygon-with-holes triangulation, subject segmentation, a renderer or a physics solver. The triangulation covers the convex hull and may bridge concave boundaries or holes. Use an appropriate boundary-aware triangulator, clipping strategy or separate domains when needed. For Voronoi cells, search or higher-level traversal, consider the documented d3-delaunay wrapper. Scientific interpolation and semantic network interpretation are separate tasks.
recommended_stack.color_guidance: Use the approved palette and stable color-role mappings. Triangulation does not authorize recoloring source images, adding random face colors or interpolating discrete scientific categories. Preserve material appearance and limited-color constraints.
recommended_stack.style_application: Optionally build a limited triangular motif from deterministic moving points. Choose stable connectivity or deliberate retriangulation events; keep the structural theme, palette and reading areas coherent.

recommended_stack.name: p5.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally create procedural drawings, generative patterns and animated Canvas or WebGL visual layers.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Use browser-mounted instance mode to isolate sketches and avoid global callbacks. Pin a compatible p5 version and check its asset-loading and redraw completion APIs. Disable autonomous playback with noLoop(). Set an explicit requested composition time before each redraw and wait for drawing and asset readiness before capture. Derive state from that time, not millis(), deltaTime, frameCount or draw-call count. Seed noise and random generation, precompute stable per-object parameters, and reset or replay stateful simulations deterministically. Seeding once alone does not guarantee out-of-order frame equivalence. Clear and rebuild frames or use verified caches for accumulated trails. Set pixel density and backing resolution deliberately. Remove the instance and release owned resources on teardown.
recommended_stack.constraints: p5.js supplies a visual layer, not the video framework, automatic physics, genuine hand-drawn poses or guaranteed export synchronization. Retain HyperFrames as primary and Remotion as conditional fallback. Keep existing palette tokens, approved colors, motion guidance and exposure cadence. Prefer existing suitable Canvas, SVG, PixiJS or Three.js code over an unnecessary additional renderer. Sound-reactive work needs a separate verified audio-analysis route and cached time-indexed analysis; do not assume sound APIs belong to core p5.
recommended_stack.verification: Compare repeated, backward and out-of-order redraws with sequential frames. Inspect decoded video for aliasing, temporal flicker, output resolution, palette fidelity and media synchronization.
recommended_stack.style_application: Build procedural patterns, particles, waves and noise-driven motion with authored pacing and controlled complexity.

recommended_stack.name: Anime.js
recommended_stack.runtime: browser for DOM/SVG; numeric object animation where supported by the selected runtime
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally animate CSS, DOM attributes, SVG geometry and numeric objects with timelines, easing, staggered sequences, line drawing and motion paths.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Use documented Anime.js v4 imports and verify the installed version; do not mix legacy anime()/anime.timeline() examples with v4 APIs. Build paused animations with explicit fixed initial and target values. Map shared composition time to the configured Anime.js time unit, which is milliseconds by default. Seek the optional child animation from the framework-controlled time adapter and verify updates reach the renderer before capture. Preserve the registered HyperFrames GSAP master timeline; an Anime.js timeline is not a drop-in substitute for that contract. Prefer GSAP when a verified adapter is unavailable. Use one animation owner per property; do not have GSAP, Motion and Anime.js write the same transform. Load fonts and geometry before constructing animations, precompute random parameters, and perform lifecycle cleanup using the documented API for the installed version.
recommended_stack.constraints: Anime.js does not generate illustration assets, solve physical simulations or render video itself. SVG morphing, motion paths and line drawing apply to their documented supported geometry; do not treat them as general 3D topology operations. Springs and overshoot are optional authored choices, not automatic smoothness improvements. Live scroll or dragging belongs to interactive delivery; author equivalent time-driven actions for video. Avoid callback-dependent state changes that fail direct or backward seeking. Preserve palette tokens, shared_motion_guidance and intentional stepped cadence. HyperFrames remains primary and Remotion conditional fallback.
recommended_stack.verification: Verify fixed initial states, exact final copy, geometry integrity, property ownership and time-unit conversion. Compare repeated, backward and out-of-order seeking with sequential playback, then inspect the decoded video for smoothness, readability, palette fidelity and loop continuity.
recommended_stack.style_application: Coordinate abstract shapes and numeric scene parameters with authored timing; renderer-specific drawing remains separate.

recommended_stack.name: Paper.js
recommended_stack.runtime: browser Canvas; Node.js geometry or asset preparation only with verified compatible DOM/Canvas dependencies for the required operation
recommended_stack.purpose: Construct and manipulate vector paths, Bezier curves, groups, clipping geometry and boolean shapes; render on Canvas or prepare SVG assets.

suggested_methods.name: Bezier path construction and sampling
suggested_methods.application: Prepare curved contours and sample positions or tangents along path length for reveals and movement.

suggested_methods.name: Path boolean operations
suggested_methods.application: Combine or cut closed shapes; inspect geometry, holes and edge cases before rendering.

suggested_methods.name: Compatible path interpolation
suggested_methods.application: Morph prepared contours with matching geometry structure; correspondence remains an authoring responsibility.

suggested_methods.name: Optional path smoothing and simplification
suggested_methods.application: Apply only when appropriate; compare against the original contour because these operations alter geometry.

recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Prefer ordinary JavaScript with an isolated PaperScope rather than installing constructors onto window or relying on PaperScript compilation. Initialize the scope on an owned Canvas after browser mount. Keep immutable rest geometry and evaluate transforms, segments and handles at requested composition time; do not repeatedly mutate the previous frame. Disable automatic view updates and autonomous onFrame playback for export, then call view.update() after applying each time state. Preload fonts and imported assets, verify SVG import completion and supported features, cache expensive boolean results, and remove temporary items and owned projects on teardown. Use existing GSAP or another verified adapter for shared time without competing property ownership. Set logical Canvas size and output pixel density explicitly.
recommended_stack.constraints: Paper.js is a 2D vector geometry and rendering library, not a paper material generator, physical fluid solver, 3D engine or video framework. Path interpolation requires compatible segment structures; matching counts alone does not ensure meaningful correspondence. Boolean operations may create compound paths or change topology. SVG import/export requires fidelity checks for unsupported source features, font handling and raster content. Preserve approved palette tokens, source geometry, shared_motion_guidance and intentional exposure cadence; optional smoothing must not erase sketch character. HyperFrames remains primary and Remotion conditional fallback. Prefer existing native SVG, Canvas or another suitable dependency when Paper.js adds no needed geometry capability.
recommended_stack.verification: Check contour fidelity, winding, holes, intersections, morph intermediate states, SVG round-trip appearance and output scale. Compare repeated, backward and out-of-order frame requests with sequential playback and inspect decoded video for palette fidelity, flicker and line quality.
recommended_stack.style_application: Animate parameterized curves and geometric compositions from fixed key states and shared composition time.

tech.implementation: Use reusable shape groups and shared coordinates for repetition and assembly. Use an existing path-interpolation library for complex morphing.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Abstract Motion Graphics without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

style.executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a Abstract Motion Graphics video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Follow {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} and save deliverables to {{output_directory}}.
Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export only. If omitted, resolve it to tech.framework_selection.default. Check the primary framework first; use tech.framework_selection.fallback only when the documented fallback_condition is met, and record the verified reason. An existing React project alone is not sufficient reason to switch.
1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Build a continuous visual system from a few shapes and limited colors with deliberate proportions and centers of gravity. Use repetition, division, merging, rotation, and varied timing; let each state lead into the next. Avoid unrelated particles or light effects that weaken the structural motif. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Use reusable shape groups and shared coordinates for repetition and assembly. Use an existing path-interpolation library for complex morphing. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional mo.js effects: consult the @mojs/core entry in tech.recommended_stack when shape, burst, swirl or HTML effects support the scene. Follow its style_application, integration_guidance, determinism_guidance and color_guidance. Preserve the resolved palette and reading holds. Build effects once, pause independent playback, and drive progress from shared composition time; verify direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks. Keep one owner per animated property and preserve the selected video framework lifecycle. Do not use live click triggers or regeneration during video export. Use the existing GSAP/SVG route if an effect cannot satisfy deterministic seeking.
Optional triangular geometry: consult Delaunator in tech.recommended_stack when a 2D triangle mesh supports the scene. Follow its style_application, input_guidance, integration_guidance, animation_guidance and color_guidance. Choose a boundary strategy and stable connectivity or deliberate retriangulation; preserve approved palette roles and source data. Render the resulting geometry separately with SVG, Canvas, PixiJS or suitable Three.js geometry. Derive point states from shared composition time and verify direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks, face quality and color continuity. Do not claim arbitrary 3D meshing, boundary-constrained triangulation, scientific interpolation or semantic relationships from Delaunator alone.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
p5.js option: If useful, select the p5.js entry in tech.recommended_stack for the visual layer. Build procedural patterns, particles, waves and noise-driven motion with authored pacing and controlled complexity. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification, and use the selected framework composition time for redraws. Keep all approved palette colors and existing style cadence unchanged.
Anime.js option: Optionally select Anime.js from tech.recommended_stack when its documented animation features help the scene. Coordinate abstract shapes and numeric scene parameters with authored timing; renderer-specific drawing remains separate. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Retain the selected framework render_pipeline and the HyperFrames GSAP master timeline contract; use Anime.js only through a verified time adapter with separate property ownership. Preserve palette tokens, exact copy, shared_motion_guidance and style cadence.
Paper.js option: Optionally select Paper.js from tech.recommended_stack when vector path geometry or Canvas rendering is useful. Animate parameterized curves and geometric compositions from fixed key states and shared composition time. Follow its suggested_methods, integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Evaluate geometry from fixed rest states at composition time, explicitly update the view, and preserve palette tokens, original contour character, style cadence and the selected framework render_pipeline.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider a fixed hero stage whose internal composition separates, expands, and shifts from centered to peripheral copy without a cut. Adapt the example objects to the topic. Pin the stage rather than freezing every internal subject.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider a cohesive orb deformed through bounded vertex displacement or compact metaballs. Keep the form connected and time-evaluated. Energy styling, blue, and glow are optional; this visual treatment does not establish physical fluid behavior.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

A punctuation circle can become the next geometric state while retaining center and continuity. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

A single central mark with a limited set of rings and rays fits repeated geometric transformation; particles must belong to the motif. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read the actual illustration and complete pattern description, motion_sequence and video_adaptation. Identify which scene elements implement that action. Reject unsupported geometry, absent subjects, unintended depth, broken contact points or unrelated interactions. Select none when no candidate fits; use restrained style-native motion instead. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

Preserve exact anchors; improve balance through area, spacing and placement rather than hue substitution. Gradient samples and material lighting are not extra base-color licenses.
palette.agent_instruction: Resolve colors in this order: task-provided exact palette, established brand or approved source palette, existing semantic color mappings, then this optional example. Read visual_cues and palette.constraints. Preserve approved anchor values, color families, ink counts and asset colors. Use chroma-js for validation, equivalent normalization and contrast assessment; evaluate gradients only when enabled and appropriate. Select readable token pairs from contrast_checks, otherwise move text onto an existing contrasting backing. Record the resolved tokens and inspect actual composited frames before rendering.

audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of Abstract Motion Graphics, suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. productionPolicy.principle: Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique.
productionPolicy.style_renderer: Owns visual construction: drawing, geometry, materials, lighting, typography, masks, textures, and specialist asset generation. Use the style-specific recommended technologies and implementation guidance.
productionPolicy.motion_engine: Owns trajectories, transforms, easing, transitions, deformation, and simulation. Select engines or algorithms appropriate to the action, with one owner for each animated property.
productionPolicy.render_pipeline: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.
productionPolicy.integration: Visual and motion layers expose deterministic state at composition time, or supply baked assets or frame sequences. The pipeline supplies seekable time and composes their output. Timeline registration and frame hooks are integration adapters, not substitutes for style-specific rendering or motion.
productionPolicy.selection: Choose only needed stack entries. A technology may serve multiple roles, but document its actual responsibility. Optional authoring, interaction, color, and preprocessing tools are not mandatory renderers or motion engines.

motionReferences.name: Scroll-Driven Pinned Hero Recomposition
motionReferences.description: The hero stage remains pinned while its internal composition transforms continuously. In the public example, hands separate from their meeting point, a ring enlarges, the central headline clears, and text fragments arrive in the corners. The stable anchor is the stage; the hero's internal objects may move.
motion_sequence: Establish a pinned hero stage with a central subject arrangement and headline.
Separate selected internal elements, enlarge a focal ring or equivalent form, and clear the centered headline.
Bring supporting text into corner or peripheral positions to complete a new arrangement without a cut, then hold and release the pinned stage when the page continues.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Keep the stage fixed in the video canvas while keyframing its internal elements through the recomposition. The main objects may separate, scale, or relocate; do not freeze them merely because the stage is pinned. Preserve framework clip timing and readable text windows.

motionReferences.name: Radial Logo Burst
motionReferences.description: Stage a central mark, repeated outward white circular waves at a deliberate pulse tempo, coordinated rays and a compact party-popper burst of white and dark squares, triangles, circles and crosses. Keep tumbling confetti close around the icon; a strong sudden forward impulse toward the viewer slows into a very brief airborne hang, then a natural gravity-driven fall, never a canvas-wide distribution. Use an expanding circular mask for palette inversion while retaining the mark center. Let the burst decay into a stable logo hold; keep later particles subordinate. Use the icon center as the popper exit: pieces begin tiny at that point, shoot forward toward the viewer with a small spread around the center, never an upward launch, increase in apparent size, overlap in front of the icon, briefly hang and then fall. Keep the burst compact; express depth with coherent perspective scale and layer ordering.
motion_sequence: Establish one centered approved mark and its initial field.

Release successive soft circular waves from the fixed mark center at regular beat intervals. Emit a compact cluster of varied white and dark confetti shapes around the icon: a powerful quick forward launch toward the viewer, rotation and tumbling, a very short airborne hang, then a natural accelerating downward fall. Keep confetti local to the icon even as waves expand beyond it. Use the icon center as the popper exit: pieces begin tiny at that point, shoot forward toward the viewer with a small spread around the center, never an upward launch, increase in apparent size, overlap in front of the icon, briefly hang and then fall.
